chunks: for Allāh, the Glorified, has made this world for what is to come hereafter, and put its inhabitants to trial as to which of you is good in action,
and we have not been created for this world, nor ordered to strive for it, but we have been made to stay in it to stand trial therein.
So, Allāh has tried me with you and tried you with me. He has therefore made either of us a plea for the other.
Now, you have leapt on the world by a wrong interpretation of the Qur’ān, and wanted me to account for what neither my hand nor tongue was responsible,
but you and the Syrians put the blame on me, and your scholar incited against me the ignorant and one who is sitting incited the one who is standing.

key_terms.لِمَا بَعْدَهَا: for what is to come hereafter (the afterlife)

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali describe the purpose of the world and his rivalry with Muawiya?
ai.summary: In this letter to Muawiya, Imam Ali (AS) establishes the cosmological purpose of the world as a testing ground for distinguishing the best in conduct, contrasting it with the transient pursuit of power. He critiques Muawiya’s political maneuvering as a distortion of Quranic exegesis used to justify worldly dominion, while noting how the Umayyad-aligned scholars mobilized the masses of Syria against the rightful Imam. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of the Fitna as a struggle between true divine authority and political expediency disguised as religious legitimacy.
